clue.text: Attachment for Sam, say, that's vital for Twist — and Pip, evidently?

indicators.note: what is vital for these words lies at their heart, so the answer is buried within the letters that follow

explanation.surface: A literary riddle about Dickens's orphans Oliver Twist and Pip, and something essential to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's vital for' signals letters lying inside 'Twist — and Pip, evidently'. Sam is Fireman Sam, the children's TV firefighter: firefighters fix a standpipe to a hydrant. Twist and Pip pull the mind towards Dickens.
explanation.definitionFit: A standpipe is the vertical fitting a firefighter connects to a street hydrant to draw water, so it is kit Fireman Sam would use.

clue.text: Rock hit — pals in it pass out

definitions.text: Rock hit — pals in it pass out

indicators.note: to rock something is to shake it about, so these three letters are jumbled
out here means disordered or wrong, so this longer run of letters is rearranged

explanation.surface: A rock song so loud that the friends inside the venue faint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' scrambles HIT and 'out' scrambles PALS IN IT PASS. The whole clue also describes the film, a spoof about a heavy-metal band whose fans might well pass out.
explanation.definitionFit: This Is Spinal Tap is the celebrated 1984 rock mockumentary, a cult hit about a hopeless heavy-metal band.

clue.text: Arm raised, make out lump

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising something turns it to read upwards

parts.note: a gun is an arm, a weapon
to make out something is to understand or get it

explanation.surface: Someone lifts an arm and spots a lump.
explanation.definitionFit: A nugget is a small rough lump, especially of gold found in the ground.

clue.text: Centre of mass that's important to see

definitions.text: Centre of mass that's important to see

parts.words: Centre of mass that's important to see
parts.note: reads like physics or sightseeing, but mass is a religious service and a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: A physics remark about a centre of mass, or a tourist sight worth visiting.
explanation.walkthrough: Mass is the Eucharistic service and a see is the area a bishop oversees; the local church where mass is said matters to the diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish church is the main place of worship of a parish, a unit within a bishop's diocese where services are held.

clue.text: Cotton on tick

parts.note: reads like buying fabric on credit, but to cotton on is to realise and a tick is a moment

explanation.surface: Buying cotton on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: To cotton on is to grasp something at last, and a tick is a brief instant: the instant of sudden realisation.

clue.text: See 21/See 26?

parts.note: these look like pointers to other grid entries, but 21 is NUMBER and 26 is LETTER, so they say 'see number' and 'see letter'; both are typographic symbols

explanation.surface: Two of the cross-references that run through this puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading the referenced entries gives 'See number' and 'See letter': pointers to a number or a letter, each a character.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters and numerals are both characters, so an instruction to see one is a reference to a character, the testimonial's name.

clue.text: Add pounds in wage increase overseen by a polymath

indicators.note: in a down entry, being overseen by something means having it placed above
the adding and the pounds go into the pay rise

parts.note: a rise is a pay increase
to tot up is to add
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A clever person tops up a pay rise with some extra money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overseen by a' puts A on top of RI(TOT L)SE in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle, the Greek philosopher, wrote on logic, biology, politics and poetry: the classic example of a polymath.

clue.text: Argentine defence — unique pictures?

parts.note: 'the', stressed as in 'the place to be', marks something as the one and only
argent is silver in heraldry, so argentine means silvery
a screen is a protective shield

explanation.surface: A defensive set-up from Argentina, perhaps on the football pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Argentine looks like the nationality but means silvery, from the heraldic argent.
explanation.definitionFit: The silver screen is a nickname for the cinema and its films, the pictures, after the reflective screens of early theatres.

clue.text: See 4
Game for kids? Poor organiser's nursing injured groin

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so the first jumble holds the second inside it
something poor is badly made, so these letters are rearranged
an injured part is damaged, so these letters are rearranged too

explanation.surface: An incompetent party organiser is tending a groin strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' and 'injured' are both anagram signals, and 'nursing' means holding: the scrambled organiser's letters hold the scrambled groin. The question mark flags a game that is a rhyme, not a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Ring-a-ring o' roses is the nursery-rhyme circle game young children play, all falling down at the end.

clue.text: See 10
Inscribed with Irish words, touch the old stone

indicators.note: something inscribed with words has them written into it, so the Irish goes inside

parts.note: tig is the playground chasing game also called tag or touch
ye is an archaic spelling of the
Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland

explanation.surface: An antique stone carved with Irish words, which one touches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inscribed with' puts the Irish language inside the other two pieces. Tig is a British name for the playground chasing game of tag.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiger's eye is a golden-brown banded quartz used as a semi-precious gemstone.

clue.text: Train maker of shoes in different sizes

indicators.note: the shoemaker sits within the size letters

parts.note: S and L are the clothing-size abbreviations small and large
Jimmy Choo is a luxury shoe designer

explanation.surface: A shoemaker training apprentices to make shoes in different sizes.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to train or teach them, a verb sense.

clue.text: See 2
Old element's edge broke

definitions.note: an adjective, meaning of or like the old element

parts.note: a brim is the edge of a cup or hat
stony, short for stony-broke, means penniless

explanation.surface: An old element's edge has been broken.
explanation.walkthrough: Brimstone is the old name for sulphur, so 'Old element's' means of brimstone; 'broke' is penniless, not damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: Brimstony is the adjective from brimstone, the biblical name for sulphur, a chemical element.

clue.text: See 6
Is this a little linear? Curvilinear

definitions.text: Is this a little linear? Curvilinear

indicators.note: a little of the following words is a short stretch of their letters

explanation.surface: A geometry puzzle: can a curved thing be slightly straight?
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles 'lineAR? Curvilinear'; and a little of a curving line is exactly what the answer is.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc is a section of a curve, such as part of a circle's circumference.

clue.text: Pah! Pap! Then, after experiencing 5, ___!

indicators.note: 5 down is a penny-drop moment; P stands for penny, so letting the pennies drop removes every P

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses an idea as rubbish, then suddenly gets it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after experiencing 5' drops each P (penny) from PAH PAP, leaving AH A: just what anyone says when the penny drops.
explanation.definitionFit: Aha is the cry of sudden understanding or discovery.

clue.text: Line from radio programme on which luvvies should appear?

definitions.text: programme on which luvvies should appear?

indicators.note: what comes over the radio is heard rather than read, so the word for line is said

parts.note: a queue is a line of people waiting

explanation.surface: A line taken from a radio show that theatrical types should appear on.
explanation.walkthrough: Luvvies are actors, in British slang; 'programme' is the misdirection, standing for a signal that sets things going, not a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue is the signal, often another actor's line, telling a performer to come on stage or speak.

clue.text: A stroke of literary genius the author promptly included in book

definitions.text: A stroke of literary genius the author promptly included in book

parts.words: A stroke of literary genius the author promptly included in book
parts.note: a stroke is a seizure suffered in a novel; the author is TOM SHARPE, from SHARP (promptly) included in TOME (book)

explanation.surface: Praise for a writer who swiftly added a brilliant touch to a book.
explanation.walkthrough: The novel's title names the stroke the Master of a Cambridge college suffers; the clue's second half encodes its author, Tom Sharpe, without giving the answer's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Porterhouse Blue is Tom Sharpe's comic novel, the title being the college term for the apoplectic fit it features.

clue.text: Take kiss from top primate

indicators.note: taking something away removes it
names what the kiss is removed from

parts.note: the apex is the top or summit
X is the conventional sign for a kiss

explanation.surface: A command to snatch a kiss from the leading primate.
explanation.definitionFit: An ape, such as a gorilla or chimpanzee, belongs to the primate order of mammals.

clue.text: See 23
See 26
Rating in engine room marrying Commander Brown and Nurse Brown?

indicators.note: marrying joins the two pairs into one

parts.note: OC stands for officer commanding
tan is a light brown
EN is an enrolled nurse
umber is a dark brown earth pigment

explanation.surface: A naval sailor in the engine room wedding two shipmates who share the surname Brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rating' looks like a naval sailor but is a fuel grade measured for the engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A petrol's octane number grades its resistance to knocking, the figure that matters inside a car engine.

clue.text: See 8
Reminder for November to turn up moonshine

parts.note: the poppy is worn in Britain in November to remember the war dead
to cock is to turn upwards, as with a hat brim or an ear

explanation.surface: A prompt to raise strong illicit spirit for November.
explanation.walkthrough: Moonshine here is nonsense, not bootleg liquor; Remembrance Day falls on 11 November.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonshine can mean foolish talk, just as poppycock is nonsense.

clue.text: For reading at the breakfast table, will this prove incisive, dear?

definitions.text: For reading at the breakfast table, will this prove incisive
definitions.meaning: a paper knife slits envelopes open, cutting into the morning post

explanation.surface: Someone at breakfast wonders whether the morning post will be cutting.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter opener is both a blade for slitting envelopes and the salutation that begins correspondence.

clue.text: Back on books, first to last, new and old

indicators.note: the opening letter is shifted to the end of the word

parts.note: green means new or inexperienced
aged means old

explanation.surface: A returning employee, rotated from first to last, novice and veteran at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to last' moves the G of GREEN to the end, making REENG.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone re-engaged has been taken on again, so is back on the payroll.

clue.text: Couples in scar unit call for bruise application

indicators.note: only a pair of letters from inside each of the three words is kept, the rest being dropped

explanation.surface: A medical unit in charge of scars is told to treat a bruise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couples in' keeps two letters per word, and which two shifts: the end of scAR, the middle of uNIt, the start of CAll. Everything else goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnica is a herbal cream or gel commonly rubbed on bruises.

clue.text: RCS visited by the Head of the 13?

indicators.note: a place visited by someone has them come inside

parts.note: the Royal College of Surgeons is the RCS, so it stands for its members

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A medical college receives a visit from the headteacher of the school.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is SCHOOL, here a group of fish rather than of pupils; the question mark marks sturgeons as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish swim in shoals called schools, and sturgeons are fish, so they might form one.
